title: Tech stocks pull U.S. markets lower, Anthropic shares fall

image.caption: Stocks on the tech-heavy Nasdaq exchange fell on Friday, the day after Anthropic's historic IPO booked double-digit gains. (CP/AP images)

blocks.text: U.S. markets are pushing lower on Friday, including Anthropic shares on their second day of trading.
U.S. stocks are sliding the day after Anthropic's blockbuster IPO
Stocks are wobbling on Wall Street and Bay Street as a retreat in artificial intelligence shares contrasts with a modest rebound in consumer staples and Canadian telecoms.
The S&P 500 index shed 1.2 per cent on Friday, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 62 points, or 0.1 per cent. The Nasdaq composite slumped 2.3 per cent.
In Toronto, the S&P/TSX Composite index is down by less than one per cent. Canada's benchmark index has slipped about eight per cent since hitting an all-time high in August.
On Friday, BCE and Telus were among the most influential stocks as investors digest news about proposed consolidation deals in Canada's telecom sector.

On the Nasdaq, Anthropic slipped over 10 per cent in a reversal from its big market debut on Thursday. The company behind the popular Claude chatbot was pitched to investors as a pure play on the AI boom.
Unlike the other AI "hyperscalers" on the market — such as Google and Meta — Anthropic's business is solely focused on building and selling AI models.
The company's Nasdaq-listed stock ended its first trading day on Thursday with a 17 per cent gain.
AI stocks have been losing ground recently, due in part to worries among investors that their market values and massive spending are unjustified.
Nvidia is among the heaviest weights on the market on Friday, falling about six per cent. Shares of Intel and SpaceX are also among the most influential decliners.

Tech stock analyst Dan Ives says the fear and anxiety behind today's tech stock sell-off is akin to levels seen during the COVID-19 pandemic and U.S. President Donald Trump's so-called "Liberation Day" tariff announcement last year.

Ives points to a "perfect storm" of factors roiling the tech trade. These include the leadership crisis at Nvidia, U.S. regulators putting tighter controls on China's access to AI chips and fears of a data centre slowdown in the U.S. driven by the "blue wave" of Democrat victories in the recent midterm elections.

items: Anthropic's stratospheric IPO fails to calm market fears over AI

blocks.text: "This is a painful tech sell-off that is heavily discounting this fourth Industrial Revolution thesis will take place over the next few years … and that is the wrong move in our view," he wrote in a note to clients on Friday.

Jeff Lagerquist is a senior writer with CBC News based in Toronto. Originally from Erin, Ont., he studied journalism at Toronto Metropolitan University. Jeff previously worked as a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance Canada. He was also a reporter and digital producer for CTV National News, BNN Bloomberg and The Financial Post. In 2025, he was a Columbia University energy journalism fellow.
